output.summary: KEP-2926 relaxes Job update validation so that node affinity, node selector, tolerations, schedulingGates, annotations and labels of a Job's pod template can be mutated while the Job is suspended and has never been unsuspended. This lets a higher-level queue controller inject placement directives before unsuspending the Job. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale:
Once a Job is unsuspended, a queue controller has no influence on where its pods land, and the scheduler is pod-centric. Allowing scheduling directives to change before the Job starts lets the queue controller steer placement while leaving pod-to-node assignment to kube-scheduler. The job-controller has no dependency on these directives, so the change is limited to update validation.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Allow mutating pod affinity, topology spread, and label selectors as well
alternatives.why_not: The reviewer argued label selectors should not be updatable and that pod affinity and topology spread are workload-specific constraints, not something a queue controller should influence. Tolerations were judged possibly unnecessary.

alternatives.option: Allow mutating scheduling directives of jobs that have started at least once
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal: it would not allow queue controllers to support preempting jobs and rescheduling them on a different partition. The KEP says this can be addressed in the future.

alternatives.option: Gate the feature only on SuspendJob rather than a separate feature gate
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers discussed this; ahg-g preferred separate gates, since the suspend field already exists and defaults to false, so validation can depend on it plus the new flag.

evidence.quote: This is a proposal to relax update validation on jobs that have never been unsuspended to allow mutating node scheduling directives
Allow mutating scheduling bits of jobs that started at least once. This will not allow queue controllers to support preempting jobs and schedule them on a different partition of the cluster.
Label selector shouldn't be updatable, in general it is discouraged to actually set it, and it is autogenerated by the job controller.
I feel this is a lot less common than the one where we allow it for any suspended job and it is something we can live with until we refactor the job controller.
the docs state the semantics clearly: "This is allowed only for suspended Jobs that have never been unsuspended before."
